title: UK DMO short conventional gilt auction — moved forward a day to Tuesday 10-27 so it clears before the Budget
source: EST: dmo.gov.uk/media/5kek12uu/sa170826.pdf — UK Debt Management Office auction schedule notice (file 'sa170826', i.e. the 17 August 2026 issue), retrieved direct 2026-10-16 (PDF, 214 KB, text layer decoded locally). The October-December gilt auction table lists 'Tuesday 27 October — A short conventional gilt' with footnote 5, which reads verbatim: 'This auction was previously scheduled for Wednesday 28 October 2026. Due to the timing of the Budget on 28 October 2026 the auction has been moved to Tuesday 27 October 2026.' The gilt stock, size and 10:00 London results time are NOT in the notice (stock named at the DMO's later quarterly announcement) and are not asserted here. Filed estimate: this lane may not self-confirm what it discovered in-sweep, and the calendar's confirmed-prefix list has no slot for the DMO
notes: PROPOSED BY uk-autumn-budget-2026-10-28 AT ITS 2026-10-16 D-12 PULSE. It is the one scheduled gilt-supply test that sits inside the Budget's own tail window: the DMO moved it off Budget day (28 Oct) to the day before, so the market's last read on gilt demand before the Chancellor speaks is this auction. Tail-bid or tail-size results on a day when the 10-year gilt is near 5.2-5.4% (highest since 2008, press-reported) would be the earliest sign that the gilt-to-Treasury channel (the parent ledger's R-squared 0.308 pipe) is opening ahead of the Budget rather than after. The parent ledger's falsifier is IGLT.L at or below -1.30% on the day; this auction is a leading read on that, not a trade. Attribution: 27 Oct also carries US 5y auction, Consumer Confidence, Durable Goods and MSFT's print, so a US move that day is not the gilt's by default. No position is or will be sized to this: symbols [], low impact, estimate-dated.
